chunks: Ghayba of al-Tabari (or al-Tusi): Al-Kulayni, from Sa'd, from al-Yaqtini, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Nafi, from Harun ibn Kharija, who said:

Harun ibn Sa'd al-Ijli said to me: 'Ismail [ibn Ja'far] is dead, towards whom you were stretching your necks [expecting him to be the Imam], and Ja'far is an old man who will die tomorrow or the day after, so you will remain without an Imam!' I did not know what to say, so I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of his words. He said: 'Far off, far off! Allah has refused, by Allah, for this matter [Imamate] to cease until the night and day cease. So when you see him, say to him: This is Musa ibn Ja'far; he will grow up, we will marry him off, and a child will be born to him as a successor, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ: Ismail ibn Ja'far, a son of the Imam who was expected to succeed him
key_terms.خَلْفاً: A successor or one who comes after
key_terms.غَيْبَةُ الطَّابِسِيِّ: Ghayba of al-Tabari (or al-Tusi), referring to the book on the occultation
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنُ جَعْفَر: Musa ibn Ja'far (Imam Musa al-Kazim), the predicted successor

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq say about the succession of Imam Musa al-Kazim?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Ghayba addresses the specific historical anxiety of the Shia community following the death of Ismail ibn Ja'far, who was widely expected to succeed, and the advanced age of Ja'far al-Sadiq. The Imam reassures them that the Imamate will not cease, predicting that Musa ibn Ja'far will grow up, be married, and produce a successor, thereby continuing the line of Imams. This narrative underscores the doctrine of 'Nass' (explicit designation) and the continuity of divine authority despite the apparent disappearance or death of prominent Imams.
